failures.title: BMW N52B30 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Valve stem seal wear - oil consumption and blue smoke
items.whatHappens: The N52B30's valve stem seals harden and lose their sealing ability over time, leading to excessive oil consumption and blue smoke on startup. Consumption of 1 litre per 500 miles is not uncommon on affected engines. Symptoms include a puff of blue smoke when starting from cold, rising oil consumption, and fouled spark plugs.
items.repairVsReplace: Valve stem seals can be replaced without removing the cylinder head using specialist tools (around 12-15 hours labour). This is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement and should be the first port of call for oil consumption issues on an otherwise healthy engine. Read our full valve stem seal failure guide

items.title: Valvetronic motor and eccentric shaft wear
items.whatHappens: The N52's Valvetronic II system uses an electric motor and eccentric shaft to vary valve lift continuously. The Valvetronic motor can fail, the eccentric shaft bearings can wear, and the sensor can develop faults - leading to rough idle, starting issues, and loss of power. In cold weather, the motor can seize, causing a crank-but-no-start situation.
items.repairVsReplace: The Valvetronic motor, eccentric shaft sensor and valve cover gasket are replaceable as a set (around £800-£1,200 at an independent specialist). This is a well-understood repair that does not require engine replacement.

items.title: VANOS solenoid and cam bearing ledge wear
items.whatHappens: The N52's Double-VANOS system can suffer from solenoid failure or, more seriously, cam bearing ledge wear. Symptoms include fluctuating idle, hesitation below 2,000 RPM, VANOS fault codes (2A82 intake, 2A87 exhaust), and reduced low-end torque.
items.repairVsReplace: VANOS solenoids can be cleaned or replaced (around £200-£400). If the cam bearing ledges are worn, the repair is more involved - the camshaft bearing caps may need replacement (around £800-£1,500). This is a preventative maintenance item that should be addressed before it causes timing issues.

items.title: Cooling system - water pump and thermostat
items.whatHappens: The N52 uses an electric water pump that is prone to failure. Symptoms include overheating, coolant loss, and the engine running hot without warning.
items.repairVsReplace: Electric water pump and thermostat replacement is standard maintenance on higher-mileage N52s (around £500-£800 at an independent specialist). This should be considered preventative at 80,000 miles.

failures.goodYearsLine: The N52B30 is widely regarded as one of BMW's most reliable modern engines - often described as "bulletproof" by owners. The 2005-2006 N52B30 (without direct injection) is considered more reliable than the later N53B30 that replaced it, which suffered from injector and high-pressure fuel pump issues. With proper maintenance, N52B30 engines regularly exceed 200,000 miles.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the N52B30
variants.intro: The N52B30 is a specific engine code within the N52 family. Unlike some BMW engines that fragment into many sub-codes with different hardware, the N52B30's variants are primarily distinguished by power output and market-specific tuning. The N52 family includes: - N52B30O0 - 258 hp (190 kW) @ 6,600 rpm, 300 Nm torque. Base engine with 3-Stage DISA intake manifold. Fitted to most 330i, 530i, 630i and X3 3.0si applications. This is the most common UK variant. - N52B30A - 258-272 hp. The "A" designation typically indicates European-market tuning with 3-Stage DISA. - N52B30B - 218 hp (160 kW) @ 6,100 rpm, 270 Nm torque. Lower-output variant fitted to some 525i, 325i and 730i models. - N52B30BF / N52B30AF - Regional variants for specific markets (e.g. North America) with different emissions calibration. - N52B30O1 - Higher-output 272 hp variant fitted to some X3 xDrive30i and 130i models. How to confirm your code: 1. On the engine - the N52B30 code is stamped on the engine block, below the intake manifold directly between the knock sensors. Look for "N52B30A", "N52B30B", "N52B30O0" or similar. 2. On the V5C logbook - the engine number is listed; cross-reference with BMW parts systems. 3. VIN decode - use a BMW VIN decoder; the engine type will be shown. 4. Registration lookup - enter your reg above and we'll confirm the exact fitment. Similar-looking codes it is commonly confused with: - BMW N52B25 - the 2.5-litre version of the N52 family, fitted to 325i and 525i models; shares the same architecture but smaller displacement - BMW N53B30 - the direct-injection successor; not a direct swap due to different fuel system and engine management - BMW M54B30 - the predecessor; different block material (iron vs magnesium-aluminium) and no Valvetronic

relatives.description: The N52B30 is a specific engine code within the N52 family. Unlike some BMW engines that fragment into many sub-codes with different hardware, the N52B30's variants are primarily distinguished by power output and market-specific tuning.
- N52B30O0 - 258 hp (190 kW) @ 6,600 rpm, 300 Nm torque. Base engine with 3-Stage DISA intake manifold. Fitted to most 330i, 530i, 630i and X3 3.0si applications. This is the most common UK variant.
- N52B30A - 258-272 hp. The "A" designation typically indicates European-market tuning with 3-Stage DISA.
- N52B30B - 218 hp (160 kW) @ 6,100 rpm, 270 Nm torque. Lower-output variant fitted to some 525i, 325i and 730i models.

variants.closing: Why fitting the wrong revision matters: The N52B30O0 (258 hp) and N52B30B (218 hp) are physically similar but have different DISA intake manifolds, ECU tuning, and in some cases different compression ratios. An N53B30 (direct injection) is not a direct swap due to different fuel system, injectors, and engine management. The N52's magnesium-aluminium block is also unique to this engine family.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement N52B30 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used N52B30 makes sense for lower-value E90 330i or E60 530i examples where the car itself is worth under £3,000-£4,000. The key requirement is documented service history with BMW LL-01 5W-30 or 5W-40 oil, and evidence that the valve stem seals have been addressed if over 80,000 miles. The primary risk with used units is undisclosed oil consumption from valve stem seal wear - insist on a cold start smoke test and compression check before purchase. Used units typically cost £1,500-£2,800. View used engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper N52B30 recon includes new valve stem seals, full VANOS solenoid service or replacement, Valvetronic motor inspection and replacement if worn, new valve cover gasket, new oil filter housing gasket, new water pump and thermostat, and full gasket set. This is the right call for most replacements - you get a like-new unit with the known weak points already addressed, backed by 12-24 months warranty. Reconditioned units typically cost £2,800-£3,600. View reconditioned engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-value, collectable or low-mileage E63 630i, Z4 3.0si or limited-production models where originality matters. An upgraded rebuild should include new timing chain guides, new oil pump chain, new piston rings, and a full set of bearings. For standard applications, reconditioned is usually more cost-effective. View rebuilt engines

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All engines can be supplied and fitted through our network of vetted UK BMW specialists - nationwide coverage with 12-month warranty on labour and parts. View supply & fit
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The N52B30 sits in 2000s BMWs - E90 330i (£2,000-£7,000), E60 530i (£2,000-£6,000), E63 630i (£3,000-£9,000), E83 X3 3.0si (£2,000-£5,000). A £3,500-£5,000 reconditioned engine plus £1,000-£1,500 fitting is a significant investment - for lower-value examples (sub‑£3,500 330i or 530i), a used engine with documented valve stem seal work may be more economic. For collectable 130i, Z4 3.0si or low-mileage examples, the investment is usually justified. The N52B30 is a well-supported engine with strong parts availability, making replacement a viable option for most owners who want to keep their car on the road.

items.question: What are the common problems with the BMW N52B30 engine?
items.answer: The N52B30's most common issues are valve stem seal wear (causing oil consumption and blue smoke on startup), Valvetronic motor failure, and VANOS solenoid/cam bearing ledge wear. The N52 is generally considered reliable, but these issues require attention at higher mileages. Valve stem seal replacement is the most common repair. Valvetronic motor failure can cause starting issues in cold weather. Regular maintenance is essential for longevity.

items.question: How do I know if my BMW has the N52B30 engine?
items.answer: The N52B30 is stamped on the engine block below the intake manifold, between the knock sensors. Look for "N52B30A", "N52B30B" or "N52B30O0" on the identification plate. You can also decode your VIN - BMW models with N52B30 show this engine code in parts systems. Enter your registration above for confirmation. The V5C logbook lists the engine number. BMW VIN decoders distinguish N52B30 from N53B30. The N52B30 uses port injection, not direct injection.

items.question: Is the N52B30 a reliable engine?
items.answer: Yes - the N52B30 is widely regarded as one of BMW's most reliable modern engines, often described as "bulletproof" by owners. With proper maintenance (regular oil changes using BMW LL-01 spec, cooling system attention, and preventative VANOS service), N52B30 engines regularly exceed 200,000 miles. The 2005-2006 N52B30 is considered more reliable than the later N53B30 that replaced it, which suffered from injector and HPFP issues. N52 is significantly more reliable than the N53 direct-injection engine. Valve stem seals are the main weakness but are repairable. Regular maintenance is the key to longevity.
